subject: religious-studies

items.q: Do all religious believers agree on ethical issues?
items.correct: No — believers hold a range of views within and between religions.
items.random_wrong: Ethics has nothing to do with religion.
items.why: Different theologies and interpretations lead to varied ethical conclusions.

items.correct: No — ethical theories (e.g. Natural Law, Situation Ethics, Utilitarianism) give reasoned frameworks.
items.random_wrong: Ethics means following the law only.
items.why: Normative theories provide structured ways to reason about right and wrong.

items.q: Does religious ethics never adapt to new issues?
items.correct: No — believers apply teachings to new situations, sometimes differently.
items.why: Applied ethics involves interpreting principles for contemporary questions.
